items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: His melodic and harmolodic concepts have influenced everything I’ve played and occurred ever since.

ctx.x: In applying for the grant that made that possible I’m guessing you had to verbalize or write on paper what was your intent, what is it that you were so intent on learning?

Well specifically I — well I didn’t feel like I — I was working on some sort of much more complex concepts at the time in terms of different time signatures and different ways of — which is why I studied with Steve Coleman. Just I wanted to — I needed to hang out with some people in a different realm. And I feel like I had stopped learning actually. So I’m not sure what I wanted to learn. A big part of the picture is like in 1998 was my first exposure to the music of Ornette Coleman. And that changed me forever…

I’ve been reading, I wish I was more familiar with Ornette and his concepts but I’ve been reading about it. But much of it makes me scratch my head I must admit. And so I’m going to take the opportunity to ask you to sort of explain some of it.
